data.why: The repository bundles a synchronized multimodal demo dataset (FT-ICR MS, EEM, UV-Vis, FTIR, NMR, SEC, elemental, and fused ML matrices) for pristine Lake Baikal NOM vs. BPPM sludge-lignin samples, matching exactly the formats each module's parser expects, so no synthetic data is needed.

goals: Upload an FT-ICR MS peak list and assign molecular formulas to build a Van Krevelen diagram distinguishing lignin-like from lipid/protein-like compound classes
Load EEM fluorescence matrices, run PARAFAC decomposition, and validate components with CORCONDIA and Split-Half diagnostics
Inspect UV-Vis absorption spectra to compute SUVA254, E2/E3, and estimate molecular weight via Perminova's equation
Process FTIR, NMR, SEC, and elemental data to derive lignin indices, IHSS aromatic fractions, molecular weight distributions, and NOSC/Van Krevelen classification
Fuse descriptors across all analytical modalities and run PLS-DA/OPLS-DA to classify samples as natural organic matter vs. technogenic sludge lignin, identifying VIP biomarkers
Generate a 1-click ecological passport report (HTML/Excel) summarizing the classification and supporting spectral evidence

review.summary: The tree follows ChemoSuite's actual pipeline (FT-ICR, optical and FTIR characterisation, then multiblock fusion and PLS-DA) with good tool-neutral wording, and all ten sampled screens back their nodes. It needs fixes before filing: it is missing the stated endpoint (the ecological passport), half of the eight modalities, and the OPLS-DA/sPLS-DA and validation options, and two features (f5, f10) bundle too much.
